newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on short-covering.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures settled higher across the board on Thursday as short-covering gathered force later in the day, traders said.
Prices ranged from 210 to 300 yen per tonne higher, with the benchmark November 1997 contract up 300 yen at 13,790 yen per tonne. Daily volume was 52,133 lots.
The market started the day on a firmer tone, following the higher Chicago market overnight.
"After recent sharp price falls, views that the market was oversold prompted private investors to cover shorts," a brokerage house trader said.
One trader said, however, that the market was likely to be pressured later by massive long positions, especially in the nearby months held by private investors.
"Further gains could be capped by long-liquidation," the trader said.
The spot December contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.70 per bushel at 0735 GMT, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The spot January contract of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was flat at $7.07 at 0737 GMT.
